thread.title: Mid-Day Update: US Stocks Return Early Gains as Wall Street Struggles With Global Growth Worries

title: Mid-Day Update: US Stocks Return Early Gains as Wall Street Struggles With Global Growth Worries
text:
Mid-Day Update: US Stocks Return Early Gains as Wall Street Struggles With Global Growth Worries December 13, 2018, 01:04:48 PM EDT By MT Newswires, MT Newswires Shutterstock photo
Wall Street was struggling for direction on Thursday with early gains compromised by investors' lingering worries of slower global growth and strong upside resistance in the S&P 500. Although the Dow Jones Industrial Average is holding a slim gain, it's down almost 100 points from the high, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq have drifted into negative territory.
Stocks were gaining ground mid-morning on encouraging signs of cooperation between the US and China that included overtures by Beijing to tone down its "Made in China 2025" mandate and increased imports of soybeans from the US.
But concerns about the health of the global economy continued to weigh, heightened by remarks from European Central Bank president Mario Draghi about downside risks to the European economy, compounded by lower growth and inflation projections. The euro spiralled lower before regaining some traction into the 1.130 level of support.
Economic data contributed to a modest retreat in stock futures this morning, with a larger-than-expected decline in initial jobless claims, offset by a significant decline in import and export prices. Led by an 11% drop in fuel prices, import prices plunged 1.6% to their lowest level in two years. Export prices were down 0.9% to a five-month low.
In corporate news, Apple ( AAPL ) plans to build a new $1 billion campus in Austin, TX as well as establish a foothold in Seattle, San Diego and Culver City. Shares were trading higher before the opening bell.
General Electric ( GE ) shares were higher for the first time in five days after the company said it is launching an independent $1.2 billion industrial Internet-Of-Things business, and long-time bear JP Morgan ( JPM ) raised its rating on the company to neutral from underweight.
European stocks all traded lower with Brexit and gloomy forecasts by the European Central Bank undermining investor confidence. France's CAC-40 led decliners with multi-nationals like L'Oreal and Legrand taking the heaviest losses.
Crude oil was up $0.64 to $51.79 per barrel. Natural gas was down $0.03 to $4.11 per 1 million BTU. Gold was down $2.90 to $1,247.10 an ounce, while silver was up $0.009 to $14.86 an ounce. Copper was up $0.008 to $2.78 per pound.
Among energy ETFs, the United States Oil Fund was up 1.48% to $10.98 with the United States Natural Gas Fund up 1.17% to $33.63. Amongst precious-metal funds, the Market Vectors Gold Miners ETF was down 0.24% to 20.34 while SPDR Gold Shares were down 0.23% to $117.52. The iShares Silver Trust was up 0.36% to $13.87.
